reason: Both kept the customer safe (isolate at the cooker switch, no live testing, engineer option), but Conversation 2 followed the sensible sequence - ruling out auto/timer mode and wrong function setting first - then obtained the exact model and delivered a confirmed-fit fan element with isolation and 'use an engineer if unsure' advice. Conversation 1 reached a confirmed diagnosis via the visual blister finding, which is a genuine strength, but its first reply nudged the customer to look for a glowing element while running, it never checked the timer, and its part advice was vague and partly wrong ('typically around 2400W', 'search for it') when the model was already known. Conversation 2's weakness is recommending the part on symptoms alone without asking for a visual inspection of the element, which stops it being a clear win.
